links.outcome: Under- and over-triage of CDSS urgency advice versus treating physician judgement
links.effect: Advice rated not appropriate in 8.7% (14/161); of these, 5 (35.7%) were more cautious than physician recommendation and none were less urgent (no under-triage).
links.quote: Importantly, no instances were identified in which the CDSS provided a less urgent recommendation than physicians considered appropriate, indicating that all discrepancies reflected conservative rather than unsafe guidance.

links.outcome: Physician pre-consultation review of EHR-integrated CDSS report
links.effect: Only 60 of 163 surveyed consultations (37%) involved pre-consultation report review; report was accessible but not surfaced where physicians prepare for consultations.
links.quote: Despite the positive findings among physicians who reviewed the report, only 60 of 163 surveyed consultations (37%) involved pre-consultation report review.

links.outcome: Under-triage and over-triage among urgency recommendations rated inappropriate
links.effect: Among 14 cases rated inappropriate, nine matched physician recommendations (64.3%; 95% CI 35.1–87.2), five were more cautious (35.7%; 95% CI 12.8–64.9), and none were less urgent. Physician recommendations used a simplified three-level scale.
links.quote: The CDSS recommendation coincided with the physician’s behaviour recommendation in nine cases (64.3%; 95% CI 35.1–87.2) and was more cautious in five (35.7%; 95% CI 12.8–64.9).

links.outcome: Inclusion of the treating physician’s most probable diagnosis among suggested conditions
links.effect: The physician’s most probable diagnosis was included in 80.4% (131/163; 95% CI 73.5–86.0) and omitted in 19.6% (32/163; 95% CI 14.0–26.5).
links.quote: The physician’s most probable diagnosis was included among the suggested conditions in 80.4% (131/163; 95% CI 73.5–86.0), with significant differences by specialty ( p = 0.035), but no significant variation by sex ( p = 1.000) or age group ( p = 0.191) (Supplementary Table 5 ).

links.outcome: Physician review of the assessment report before consultation
links.effect: Only 60 of 163 surveyed consultations (37%) involved pre-consultation report review despite EHR integration; the report was not surfaced where physicians typically prepared for consultations.
links.quote: Despite the positive findings among physicians who reviewed the report, only 60 of 163 surveyed consultations (37%) involved pre-consultation report review.

links.effect: Only 37% of consultations involved pre-consultation report review because it was not surfaced appropriately.
links.quote: The report was accessible but not surfaced at the point where physicians typically prepare for a consultation, meaning that even with EHR integration, the information competed with other documentation for clinician attention.

links.effect: No differences in appropriateness were observed by case specialty, sex, or age group.
links.quote: No differences were observed by case specialty ( p = 0.535), sex ( p = 0.237) or age group ( p = 1.000)
